summary: The quadric measure is the flat-chart image of a product; the fibres in the skew direction are translates, and their total mass is the quadric mass of the size-(j+5) vectors.

steps.lean:
have N := MeasurePreserving.comp ⟨by fun_prop, rfl⟩ (measurePreserving_shuffle_coords.comp (.prod
    ⟨measurable_prodMk_right, by rw [volume_pi_eq_dirac, prod_dirac]⟩ (.id _)))
steps.claim: N: regrouping the coordinates (measurePreserving_shuffle_coords) together with a Dirac mass at the empty middle block is measure preserving.

steps.lean:
⟨_, _, _, _, _, _, inferInstance, .comp ⟨by fun_prop, rfl⟩ measurePreserving_shuffle_coords,
    rfl, by tauto, measurable_measure_prodMk_left (N.1 measurableSet_vecsOfSize),
steps.claim: The witnesses: ζ and k from the flat chart of the quadric composed with the regrouping (measure preserving); the image under E^F_b is floorQuadric(F, b) by definition; k keeps the coordinate groups; μ(p) = the ζ-mass of the fibre, measurable in p.

steps.lean:
fun p w ↦
    measure_le_of_sub_mem fun y k ↦ ⟨y, fun z h ↦ by simp [flatChart, star_sumElim] at *; grind
    [mem_ofSize_mono, Size.sub_mem_ofSize, sub_mem_ofSize h.1.1 k.1.1]⟩,
steps.claim: The fibre bound: if two points z, z' of the fibre map into vecsOfSize(j+4), their difference maps into vecsOfSize(j+5) (sub_mem_ofSize), so the fibre is contained in a translate of the set of z mapping into vecsOfSize(j+5); by translation invariance its mass is at most that set's.
∫ μ = (vol × ζ)(set of points mapping into vecsOfSize(j+5)) ≤ the quadric mass of vecsOfSize(j+5) ≤ M (e).
